standards.name: IHIW XML (Workshop XML NGS HLA Typing Report) v1.4
standards.abstract: This standard defines an XML schema for reporting next-generation sequencing (NGS) HLA typing reports. The research objects are HLA genotyping reports derived from NGS assays, including locus-level GL String genotypes, consensus sequences for contiguous features, primary read data locations, quality metrics, and annotations of novel polymorphisms. The schema was developed and published for the 17th International HLA and Immunogenetics Workshop (IHIW) to capture both genotyping data and associated metadata (laboratory identifiers, instrumentation, software, reagents/protocols, reference databases, phasing and feature coordinates). The package on GitHub contains the IHIW XML Typing Report Schema (v1.4) and XSD and is intended to standardize the format and content of submitted HLA NGS typing reports.

classification.rationale: The source is an explicit XML schema listing elements and named attributes with concrete data types or formats (e.g., 'LabCode: a six character alphabetic code', 'Software_Function: (CV list: Read Processing, ...)', 'PhasingGroup: (Integer)', 'DataFileLoc: (URL, Filepath or Filename)'). Each named attribute is a discrete metadata field with a specified format, so the document presents genuine field-level structure (a metadata table/schema).

Lab.LabCode.name: LabCode
Lab.LabCode.descr: A six character alphabetic code provided by the 17WS organizers that identifies the laboratory submitting the report.
Lab.LabCode.evidence: LabCode: a six character alphabetic code provided by the 17WS organizers.

Lab.Lab_defined_ID.name: Lab_defined_ID
Lab.Lab_defined_ID.descr: An internal identifier used by the reporting laboratory to identify a given report; must allow the reporting laboratory to unambiguously identify the report.
Lab.Lab_defined_ID.evidence: Lab_defined_ID: an internal identifier used by the reporting laboratory to identify a given report. Each such laboratory identifier should allow the reporting laboratory to unambiguously identify the report.

Software_Applied.Software_Manufacturer.name: Software_Manufacturer
Software_Applied.Software_Manufacturer.descr: The manufacturer of the software applied in processing or analysis.
Software_Applied.Software_Manufacturer.evidence: Software_Manufacturer: the manufacturer of the software

Software_Applied.Software_Name.name: Software_Name
Software_Applied.Software_Name.descr: The name of the software applied.
Software_Applied.Software_Name.evidence: Software_Name: the name of the software applied

Software_Applied.Software_Parameters.name: Software_Parameters
Software_Applied.Software_Parameters.descr: Any non-default parameter settings used in the application of the software.
Software_Applied.Software_Parameters.evidence: Software_Parameters: any non-default parameter settings used in the application of the software

Software_Applied.Software_Version.name: Software_Version
Software_Applied.Software_Version.descr: The version, or other identifier, defining the software applied.
Software_Applied.Software_Version.evidence: Software_Version: the version, or other identifier, defining the software applied

Software_Applied.Software_Function.name: Software_Function
Software_Applied.Software_Function.descr: Controlled vocabulary for the function to which the software was applied (may be applied to read processing, consensus generation, or allele calling).
Software_Applied.Software_Function.evidence: Software_Function: (CV list: Read Processing, Base Calling/Consensus Generation, Allele Calling), the function to which the software was applied.

Hardware_Used.Instrument_Firmware.name: Instrument_Firmware
Hardware_Used.Instrument_Firmware.descr: The version number, or other identifier, defining the software used on the instrument for data-analysis.
Hardware_Used.Instrument_Firmware.evidence: Instrument_Firmware: the version number, or other identifier, defining the software used on the instrument for data-analysis

Hardware_Used.Instrument_Model_Number.name: Instrument_Model_Number
Hardware_Used.Instrument_Model_Number.descr: The model number, or other identifier, defining the type of instrument used for the typing.
Hardware_Used.Instrument_Model_Number.evidence: Instrument_Model_Number: the model number, or other identifier, defining the type of instrument used for the typing

Hardware_Used.Instrument_name.name: Instrument_name
Hardware_Used.Instrument_name.descr: The name of the instrument used.
Hardware_Used.Instrument_name.evidence: Instrument_name: the name of the instrument

Hardware_Used.Manufacturer.name: Manufacturer
Hardware_Used.Manufacturer.descr: The company or organization that built the instrument.
Hardware_Used.Manufacturer.evidence: Manufacturer: the company or organization that built the instrument

Reagent_Protocol.protocol_name.name: protocol_name
Reagent_Protocol.protocol_name.descr: A short description (name) of the protocol and reagents used in performing the typing.
Reagent_Protocol.protocol_name.evidence: Protocol Name: a short description of the protocol and reagents used in performing the typing

Reagent_Protocol.protocol_source.name: protocol_source
Reagent_Protocol.protocol_source.descr: The company, laboratory or other entity that developed the protocol and reagents used to perform the typing.
Reagent_Protocol.protocol_source.evidence: Protocol Source: The company, laboratory or other entity that developed the protocol and reagents used to perform the typing

Reagent_Protocol.protocol_external_ident.name: protocol_external_identifier
Reagent_Protocol.protocol_external_ident.descr: A reference to an external source that describes the protocol and reagents applied (could be a GTR entry, webpage, DOI or citation).
Reagent_Protocol.protocol_external_ident.evidence: Protocol External Identifier: A reference to an external source that describes the protocol and reagents applied. This could be a reference to a Genetic Testing Registry (GTR) entry, a laboratory or manufacturer webpage describing the protocol and reagents, a DOI or citation of a published paper that includes the protocol.

Reagent_Protocol.protocol_internal_ident.name: protocol_internal_identifier
Reagent_Protocol.protocol_internal_ident.descr: If a protocol document is uploaded, include the file-name here.
Reagent_Protocol.protocol_internal_ident.evidence: Protocol Internal Identifier: If a protocol document is uploaded, include the file-name here.

Reagent_Protocol.protocol_deviations.name: protocol_deviations
Reagent_Protocol.protocol_deviations.descr: Any changes to the referenced protocol should be noted here.
Reagent_Protocol.protocol_deviations.evidence: Protocol Deviations: Any changes to the above referenced protocol should be noted here.

Sample.SampleID.name: SampleID
Sample.SampleID.descr: An alphanumeric string that allows the reporting laboratory to unambiguously identify the sample typed; should correspond to a sample registered as part of a 17IHIWS project.
Sample.SampleID.evidence: SampleID: an alphanumeric string that allows the reporting laboratory to unambiguously identify the sample typed. This identifier should correspond to a sample already registered as part of a 17IHIWS project.

Genotyping.Genotype_GL.name: Genotype_GL
Genotyping.Genotype_GL.descr: A locus-level HLA genotype recorded using GL String format; should include all genotyping ambiguities and phase information. 'Absent' is reported for loci not present.
Genotyping.Genotype_GL.evidence: Genotype_GL: a locus-level HLA genotype recorded using GL String format, as defined by Milius et al. 2013 (doi: 10.1111/tan.12150). Use of GL Strings allows all genotyping ambiguities to be accurately reported, along with phase information between loci. All ambiguity should be reported for a given sample. If a given locus was tested for, but found to be not present in the subject typed (e.g., a subject homozygous for DRB1*01 alleles will have no DRB3, DRB4, or DRB5 genes), report 'Absent' (e.g., DRB3*Absent) for that locus in the GL String.

Genotyping.Locus.HLATyping.name: HLATyping
Genotyping.Locus.HLATyping.descr: The allele in the Genotype_GL attribute that this Locus element corresponds to.
Genotyping.Locus.HLATyping.evidence: HLATyping: (Allele in the GL String), the HLA allele specified in the Genotype_GL attribute that this Locus element corresponds to.

Genotyping.Locus.Alignment_Reference_DB.name: Alignment_Reference_DB
Genotyping.Locus.Alignment_Reference_DB.descr: The IMGT/HLA Database release version or Genome Reference Consortium release used for aligning reads for consensus generation (e.g., IMGT/HLA Database 3.18.0 or GRCh37).
Genotyping.Locus.Alignment_Reference_DB.evidence: Alignment_Reference_DB: the IMGT/HLA Database release version (e.g., IMGT/HLA Database 3.18.0) or Genome Reference Consortium release version (GRCh37) used for aligning reads for consensus generation.

Genotyping.Locus.BaseCalling_Reference_D.name: BaseCalling_Reference_DB
Genotyping.Locus.BaseCalling_Reference_D.descr: The IMGT/HLA Database release version used to identify the genotype from the consensus sequence.
Genotyping.Locus.BaseCalling_Reference_D.evidence: BaseCalling_Reference_DB: the IMGT/HLA Database release version (e.g., IMGT/HLA Database 3.18.0) used to identify the genotype from the consensus sequence.

Genotyping.Locus.Consensus_Sequence.name: Consensus_Sequence
Genotyping.Locus.Consensus_Sequence.descr: A nucleotide sequence representing a contiguous phased region of DNA; corresponds to a single feature or multiple contiguous features.
Genotyping.Locus.Consensus_Sequence.evidence: Consensus_Sequence: A nucleotide sequence representing a contiguous phased region of DNA. This can correspond to a single feature, or to multiple contiguous features.

Genotyping.Locus.Feature.name: Feature
Genotyping.Locus.Feature.descr: Identify the feature(s) (e.g., 5'-UTR, Exon1, Intron1, etc.) to which this Locus element applies; multiple contiguous features may be defined per Locus element.
Genotyping.Locus.Feature.evidence: Feature: (5’-UTR, 3’-UTR, Intron1,Intron2, Intron3, Intron4, Intron5, Intron6, Intron7, Exon1, Exon2, Exon3, Exon4, Exon5, Exon6, Exon7, Exon8), identify the feature, or specific set of contiguous features, to which this Locus element applies.

Genotyping.Locus.Locus_name.name: Locus_name
Genotyping.Locus.Locus_name.descr: The HLA locus for which the sequence data and metadata in a given Locus element are reported.
Genotyping.Locus.Locus_name.evidence: Locus_name: (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-DRB1, HLA-DRB3, HLA-DRB4, HLA-DRB5, HLA-DQA1, HLA-DQB1, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1), the HLA locus for which the sequence data and metadata in a given Locus element are reported.

Genotyping.Locus.MeanReadDepth.name: MeanReadDepth
Genotyping.Locus.MeanReadDepth.descr: The mean read depth across the length of the consensus sequence string.
Genotyping.Locus.MeanReadDepth.evidence: MeanReadDepth:  the mean read depth across the length of the consensus sequence string.  If a locus is Absent, this is not reported.

Genotyping.Locus.DataFileLoc.name: DataFileLoc
Genotyping.Locus.DataFileLoc.descr: The URL, path or name of the file containing the primary read data generated by the instrument (primary read data as unmapped reads with quality scores, e.g., FASTQ, SFF, or unmapped BAM with quality scores).
Genotyping.Locus.DataFileLoc.evidence: DataFileLoc: (URL, Filepath or Filename), the URL, path or name of the file containing the primary read data generated by the instrument. Primary read data should be reported as unmapped reads with quality scores (e.g., FASTQ, SFF, or unmapped BAM with quality scores).

Genotyping.Locus.PhasingGroup.name: PhasingGroup
Genotyping.Locus.PhasingGroup.descr: An integer (indexed at 0 for each Locus_name) that identifies Locus elements that share phase; each element for which phase is unknown gets a new PhasingGroup number.
Genotyping.Locus.PhasingGroup.evidence: PhasingGroup: (Integer), an integer(indexed at 0 for each Locus_name) that identifies Locus elements that share phase. E.g., if phase is known between all Locus elements for a given Locus-name, PhasingGroup would be either 0 or 1 for a heterozygote at the locus, and 0 for a homozygote at the locus. Each element for which phase is unknown gets a new PhasingGroup number.

Genotyping.Locus.NovelPolymorphism.name: NovelPolymorphism
Genotyping.Locus.NovelPolymorphism.descr: Description of novel sequence polymorphisms not present in the reference database using a notation that identifies the reference database version, reference allele accession, feature and difference (example notation provided).
Genotyping.Locus.NovelPolymorphism.evidence: NovelPolymorphism: describe any novel sequence polymorphisms resulting in a sequence that does not correspond to an allele in the reference database using a notation that identifies the reference database version, reference allele acccession number, feature in which the novel polymorphism is found, and difference from the referenced feature. For example, IMGT/HLA|3.18.0|HLA00001|1.4|G56C identifies a G>C transversion at position 56 of exon 2 in a sequence that is otherwise identical to the exon 2 sequence of HLA-A*01:01:01:01.

Genotyping.Locus.FeatureNumber.name: FeatureNumber
Genotyping.Locus.FeatureNumber.descr: The locus-specific number (defined by the IMGT/HLA Database) for the Feature, or set of numbers (delimited by + signs) for contiguous Features reported for this Locus Element, in contiguous order.
Genotyping.Locus.FeatureNumber.evidence: FeatureNumber: The locus-specific number (defined by the IMGT/HLA Database) for the Feature, or set of numbers, delimited by + signs, for contiguous Features reported for this Locus Element, in contiguous order.

Genotyping.GenotypeAnnotation.Annotation.name: Annotation
Genotyping.GenotypeAnnotation.Annotation.descr: Structured text annotation characterizing the result for each allele at a given locus (provides context for novel sequence variation and other annotations).
Genotyping.GenotypeAnnotation.Annotation.evidence: GenotypeAnnotation: for each allele a given locus, characterize the result of the se

Genotyping.FeatureCoordinate.FeatureNumb.name: FeatureCoordinate.FeatureNumber
Genotyping.FeatureCoordinate.FeatureNumb.descr: FeatureNumber for the feature coordinate (locus-specific number).

Genotyping.FeatureCoordinate.FeatureStar.name: FeatureCoordinate.FeatureStart
Genotyping.FeatureCoordinate.FeatureStar.descr: Start coordinate (Number) for the feature coordinate.

Genotyping.FeatureCoordinate.FeatureStop.name: FeatureCoordinate.FeatureStop
Genotyping.FeatureCoordinate.FeatureStop.descr: Stop coordinate (Number) for the feature coordinate.

standards.name: HML (Histoimmunogenetics Markup Language) 1.0.1 - 18th IHIWS Vendor Genotyping Requirements
standards.abstract: This document provides vendor-focused guidelines for reporting HLA genotyping results for the 18th IHIWS. The research objects are HLA genotyping result documents and allele/sequence data, submitted as HML 1.0.1 XML documents and GLStrings, and including sequence alignments against IPD‑IMGT/HLA reference sequences. The standard referenced is HML 1.0.1 (an XML schema from the NMDP/Milius et al. 2015), and the guidance is maintained/used by the IHIWS and associated groups (Anthony Nolan HLA Informatics Group, NMDP). It addresses the need for consistent, machine- and human-interpretable genotype reporting by defining required validation/formatting (schema conformance, MIRING, GLStrings), rules for choosing and reporting reference sequences and database release versions, and expectations for how to report novel variants and sequences outside reference regions.

classification.rationale: The source is prose guidance and a checklist of requirements and recommendations (validation rules, reference-selection guidance, versioning advice and reporting conventions). It does not present a field-level metadata table or a directed sequence-of-steps; items are instructions/recommendations rather than named data fields, so it is a PRINCIPLE-style standard.

principles.principle: Purpose: consistency and predictability in reporting for 18th IHIWS
principles.evidence: When reporting HLA genotyping for the [18th IHIWS], it is necessary to be consistent and predictable, to facilitate ease of interpretation and reusability.

principles.principle: Provide HLA genotyping data in HML 1.0.1 format (XML Schema)
principles.evidence: HLA genotyping data should be provided in the [HML 1.0.1 format](http://schemas.nmdp.org) ([Milius et al., 2015](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4674307/)). This format is described by an [XML Schema](http://schemas.nmdp.org/spec/hml/1.0.1/hml-1.0.1.xsd), and facilitates the transmission of the most important data related to the protocols, sequence, and interpretation involved in creating the genotyping result. The schema is strict in it's data format, but allows a wide variety of data to be included.

principles.principle: HML documents uploaded to the workshop database are validated
principles.evidence: HML Documents that are uploaded to the [workshop database](https://data.ihiws.org/) are validated according to some sets of standards.

principles.principle: Documents must conform to the HML Schema
Documents should follow the MIRING guidelines
principles.evidence: * Documents should follow the [MIRING](http://miring.b12x.org) guidelines ([Mack et al., 2015](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4674382/)).
* Genotypes should be reported as valid GLStrings ([Milius et al., 2013](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23849068/)).

principles.principle: HML documents are validated against the NMDP gateway
principles.evidence: * HML documents are validation against the NMDP gateway, which provides further guidelines for high quality data.

principles.principle: Present sequence data as an alignment against a known/reference sequence
principles.evidence: Sequence data should be presented as an alignment against a known sequence.

principles.principle: Use reference sequences from a provided subset of full-length alleles from a given IPD‑IMGT/HLA release
principles.evidence: Sequences must be from a subset of full-length alleles chosen from a given release of IPD-IMGT/HLA Database.

principles.principle: Report submission of known full-length allele matches as matching the IPD‑IMGT/HLA allele
principles.evidence: * Submission of known sequences that match known alleles, over the full length of the submitted sequence can be reported as matching the known allele sequence from IPD-IMGT/HLA

principles.principle: Report novel variants relative to a provided reference, using indices relative to that reference
principles.evidence: * Sequences with Novel variants should be reported against a reference from the provided list. Variants should be reported using indices relative to the chosen reference sequence.

principles.principle: If a typed allele is not on the provided reference list, report allele variants relative to one of the provided full-length IPD‑IMGT/HLA sequences and provide interpreted genotype as GLString
principles.evidence: * If the sequence is typed as a known allele, but the allele is not on the provided list of reference sequences, allele variants should be reported relative to one of the provided full-length IPD-IMGT/HLA sequences. The interpreted genotype can be provided as a GLString.

principles.principle: Report extra sequence outside reference regions as insertions at sequence ends
principles.evidence: * If the submittd sequence is reported outside the region of the reference sequence, such as in extended UTRs, the extra sequence can be reported as an insertion at the beginning or end of the reference.

principles.principle: Specify and prefer recent IPD‑IMGT/HLA database release versions (e.g., 3.39.0 or later) for submissions
principles.evidence:
HML Documents will specify the release version of the IPD-IMGT/HLA database. The chosen release should be recent, to hopefully provide some consistency in data interpretation.

* If possible, use release version 3.39.0 or later for the submission of HML documents for the 18th IHIWS
	* We will support future IPD-IMGT/HLA releases up to and including the versions released during the Workshop in May 2022.
* Reference sequences are also provided for each IPD-IMGT/HLA release since 3.26.0, mostly for historical and analysis reasons. Versions 3.26.0-3.38.0 are discouraged for the 18th IHIWS.

principles.principle: Vendors may choose reference strategy from provided list but avoid internal vendor databases; ensure results can be translated back to IPD‑IMGT/HLA
principles.evidence:
* It is valuable to use a reference sequence that is clinically similar to the reported sequence.
	* The submitter may use a reference sequence, from the provided list of full-length references, that is likely to be clinically similar to the submitted sequence.
		* Likely, this would match in exon sequences.

* Genotyping results are "simpler" if they're reported against the closest matching sequence, regardless of clinical outcomes.
	* It may be more relevant to use a full-length common allele as a reference, and perhaps easier for reporting
	* Ideally,  "variants" are reported against confirmed genotypes in glstring.
	* We would like to know where the variants are in the closest alleles. 
	* A tool is in development to provide the closest-matching sequence to a given consensus sequence. 
		* Vendors are encouraged to use their own strategy for choosing a reference sequence, from the provided list of full-length references.

* It is critical that results can be translated back to IPD-IMGT/HLA.
	* Variants are defined against the reference sequence.
	* This is why it is required to use a subset of selected alleles from a subset of database releases.
	* The use of internal vendor databases is strongly discouraged, as it makes interpretation of sequence results very difficult.
